title: infra: Add VPC control plane Terraform module — multi-AZ subnets, endpoints, peering, Route53
author: Ava Hernandez
release_notes: Adds a reusable Terraform module and environment examples for provisioning Redwood private control plane VPCs. Includes multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. Backwards-compatible: no runtime API changes.
description: Context: customers deploying Redwood Private need a repeatable, auditable Terraform module to provision VPC networking for the control plane. This PR introduces a vpc-control-plane module that provisions multi-AZ private subnets, interface endpoints (S3, ECR, KMS, STS), security groups with least-privilege defaults, cross-account VPC peering configuration hooks, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation for control-plane domain resolution. Motivation: reduce manual steps for on-prem/VPC installs, support multi-AZ high-availability, and centralize security best practices. What this PR does: - New module: terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane with main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, examples/ - Multi-AZ support: variable-driven AZ count and subnet sizing, default CIDR planning helper - Interface endpoints: optional creation of commonly required endpoints and support for additional endpoints via map variable - Security groups: minimal ingress rules, explicit egress to required endpoints, documented tags for audit logs - Peering: templates and example usage for cross-account peering and route propagation; includes one-shot peering acceptance automation via module outputs - Route53: private hosted zone delegation example and helper for creating appropriate records in the control plane account - Integration tests: lightweight terraform plan-only tests in pipeline for module examples - Docs: new docs/terraform/vpc-control-plane.md with example usage and upgrade notes Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented and documented - [x] Example env configurations for single-AZ and multi-AZ - [x] CI plan checks added to pipeline - [x] Security review (SGs and endpoints) completed - [x] Tested on internal staging account Upgrade notes: When adopting this module, existing customers should import current state (if converting from manually provisioned resources) and review subnet CIDR vars. No forced changes to existing control planes. Related: ENG-4821 (private deployment installer work), ENG-4978 (route53 delegation story).
commits: Initial module skeleton: variables and basic resource wiring
Add multi-AZ subnet creation, sizing helper, and outputs
Add interface endpoints and security group defaults
Add peering templates and example peering usage
Address review: tighten SG egress rules and add tags
CI: add plan-only test for examples and terraform fmt/lint
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Please justify why we create interface endpoints by default rather than opt-in. Reply: Ava Hernandez: Endpoints are opt-in via a boolean variable, default is false. Updated docs to clarify. (resolved)

Maya Thompson: Security group egress looks broad to 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 443/80 — can we restrict to endpoints? Reply: Ava Hernandez: tightened egress to endpoints and known NAT CIDRs where applicable; added tests that fail if broad 0.0.0.0/0 is detected. (resolved)

Ethan Zhao: Will this block rolling upgrades of control plane components? Reply: Ava Hernandez: No runtime changes. Module surfaces outputs for existing VPC IDs to allow import and seamless adoption; added upgrade_notes in docs. (resolved)
Ravi Patel: CI plan flagged a provider version constraint mismatch. Reply: Ava Hernandez: pinned provider to >=3.60, ran fmt and updated lockfile. CI now green. (resolved)
Maya Thompson: Approve after small nit on variable naming. Reply: Ava Hernandez: renamed variable and updated examples. (approved)
Ethan Zhao: Approved and performed final merge. (merged)
notes: This PR centralizes control-plane networking provisioning. Ops and Onboarding teams should coordinate rollout for existing customers migrating from manual VPCs. See docs/terraform/vpc-control-plane.md for migration steps and import examples.
